title: Packing online orders without losing the list
target: How online orders work in Supermarket Simulator: where an order lives, how it is tracked, what the notebook keeps, and how to use the map and the counter so nothing is packed twice or missed.
version: 1.6.0 (223), read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A shop with online ordering unlocked
A stocked shop to pick from
Access to the order notebook and the map

steps.do: Treat an order as a thing of its own rather than a line in a list somewhere, because orders and their data are modelled by the game.
steps.because: orders and their data are modelled by the game (Order, OrderData)

steps.do: Know where they are held, because orders sit in a container of their own with a manager over them.
steps.because: online orders are held together in a container of their own with a manager over them (OrdersContainer, OrderManager)

steps.do: Expect the order list to have data of its own and a shared form, so an order can be seen by more than one player.
steps.because: the order list has data of its own and a networked form (OrderListData, OrderNetworkData)

steps.do: Pack for the customer attached to the order rather than for a generic buyer, because an online order has its own customer.
steps.because: an online order has a customer of its own (OnlineOrderCustomer)

steps.do: Use the map when you are collecting, because an order can put a task on it.
steps.because: an online order can put a task on the map (OnlineOrderOpenMapTask)

steps.do: Handle the order at the counter rather than by looking for a menu, because there is an interaction for it.
steps.because: there is an interaction for an online order (OnlineOrderInteraction)

steps.do: In a shared shop, expect that interaction to be shared as well.
steps.because: the order interaction has a networked version (NetworkOnlineOrderInteraction)

steps.do: Read the notebook entry for a product rather than guessing at what the order wants, because the notebook keeps a product entry.
steps.because: the order notebook keeps an entry for a product (OrderNotebookProductEntry)

steps.do: Use the order interface and its document button when you need the details in front of you.
steps.because: the order interface is its own, with a document button (OrdersUI, OnlineDocButton)

steps.do: Remember that what you ship has a price of its own, because boxes carry a market price.
steps.because: boxes carry a market price of their own (BoxMarketPrice)

commonMistakes: Picking from memory instead of reading the notebook entry for the product.
Packing for a sale at the till when the order belongs to an online customer of its own.
Forgetting the map task and walking the aisles looking for something already listed.
In a shared shop, both players packing the same order because neither looked at the shared list.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
